spec: DESIGN.md — Vocabulary; issue #784 (D7–D9, D11, D14, D27); vectors/README.md — The platform-table family
description: Pairs in, the platform table's translation out, in the projection both families assert: per pair and for the intersection, every source's keys with their relation; none, unknown and conflict as stated values.

vectors.name: a-romm-slug-covers-three-es-de-systems
vectors.rationale: RomM folds the folders genesis, megadrive and megadrivejp into its genesis slug (platform_aliases.py), so the slug is broader than each ES-DE system: ES-DE answers three keys, each narrowMatch — a finer vocabulary, never uncertainty (#784 D8).

vectors.name: a-bare-folder-is-the-union-of-every-folder-vocabulary
vectors.rationale: A bare folder name means what every folder vocabulary means by it (#784 D14): ES-DE's megadrive is one system, Batocera's megadrive covers Genesis and the Japanese Mega Drive too (its platform list), so the folder alone names three ES-DE systems.

vectors.name: a-second-pair-narrows-the-folder-to-one-system
vectors.rationale: Only another pair narrows a bare folder (#784 D9, D14): with ES-DE's megadrive beside it the intersection is the one system.

vectors.name: romms-arcade-slug-covers-fourteen-rows
vectors.rationale: RomM 5.4.1 folds thirteen folders into its arcade slug, which with the slug's own arcade folder reach fourteen rows: twelve ES-DE systems and Batocera's namco22 and namco2x6, every one of them narrower than the slug.

vectors.name: two-systems-share-nothing-and-are-a-conflict
vectors.rationale: The Super Game Boy and the Game Boy Color are two systems: the pairs intersect in nothing, and the answer names both pairs as the conflict — atlas picks neither (#784 D9).

vectors.name: a-romm-only-system-has-no-key-anywhere-else
vectors.rationale: The Altair 8800 is a RomM slug no frontend, distribution, core or registry in the table names: every source but RomM's own two columns (its slug and its folder of that spelling) answers none, which is a definite answer (#784 D3).

vectors.name: a-source-the-table-does-not-hold-is-unknown
vectors.rationale: MobyGames is not a source of the table (#784 D21): the pair is unknown, stated with platform-source-unknown, which names the asked source and the table's sources (#784 D31), never guessed.

data.sources: esde, esde-platform, retrodeck, emudeck, romm, romm-folder, libretro, batocera, knulli, rocknix, igdb, screenscraper, thegamesdb

vectors.name: a-stated-source-version-the-table-does-not-hold-is-a-caveat
vectors.rationale: The client says its key comes from RomM 5.3.0; the table holds RomM at 5.4.1, so the answer is the 5.4.1 meaning with the platform-source-version-differs caveat (#784 D11).

vectors.name: rocknix-pc-is-related-to-dos
vectors.rationale: ROCKNIX's pc folder is its DOS system, not ES-DE's IBM PC system: a reviewed override relates it to ES-DE's dos (relatedMatch), so a client is told the overlap, not an identity.

vectors.name: a-combined-romm-slug-is-broader-than-two-batocera-keys
vectors.rationale: RomM's combined slug for the Sharp MZ-80B/2000/2500 line covers Batocera's mz2000 and mz2500: each Batocera key is narrower than the slug.

vectors.name: a-renamed-batocera-key-is-the-es-de-system
vectors.rationale: Batocera's jaguar is ES-DE's atarijaguar under another spelling (a reviewed rename); KNULLI's jaguar follows it onto the same row.

vectors.name: an-igdb-id-reaches-both-es-de-systems-of-its-console
vectors.rationale: IGDB 19 is RomM's IGDB record for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System. RomM's snes slug reaches ES-DE's snes alone (and Batocera's snes-msu1, which RomM folds into it); a reviewed override places the record on ES-DE's snesna as well, the same console under a second ES-DE system with the same full name. So ES-DE's snes and snesna are each narrower than 19, and so is RomM's own snes slug: the slug covers snes, the record covers snes and snesna. ES-DE's sfc is not reached: the Super Famicom is IGDB's record 58.

vectors.name: the-cd32s-ids-stay-on-the-cd32
vectors.rationale: IGDB 114 is RomM's IGDB record for the Amiga CD32. RomM resolves the folder amigacdtv to its CD32 slug, so the slug covers ES-DE's cdtv as well; ES-DE's scraper map gives the CDTV its own ScreenScraper id, and a reviewed override keeps the CD32's ids on ES-DE's amigacd32 alone. RomM's own slug still covers both, as RomM states it.

vectors.name: the-game-boy-colors-ids-stay-off-the-super-game-boy
vectors.rationale: ScreenScraper 10 is the Game Boy Color in ES-DE's scraper map and RomM's list. RomM resolves the folders sgb and sgb-msu1 to its gbc slug, which carried the id onto the Super Game Boy; ES-DE's map gives the Super Game Boy its own id 127, and a reviewed override keeps 10 on ES-DE's gbc and Batocera's two-player Game Boy Color system.

vectors.name: a-folder-only-rocknix-spells-is-still-a-folder
vectors.rationale: A bare folder name is matched against every folder vocabulary, ROCKNIX's included: pico-8 is ROCKNIX's spelling alone, and it still answers PICO-8 in every source.

vectors.name: a-folder-only-emudeck-spells-is-still-a-folder
vectors.rationale: A bare folder name is matched against every folder vocabulary, EmuDeck's included: sneshd is EmuDeck's spelling alone, a folder for one part of the SNES's games, and it answers through EmuDeck's key.
